facts.fact: Guinea's national director of political and electoral affairs said the country has a law on the identification of natural persons.
facts.system: Loi sur l'identification des personnes physiques

facts.fact: The same official said the law allows biometric data to be recorded from age 10 and a national identity card issued.
facts.system: Loi sur l'identification des personnes physiques

facts.fact: The Prime Minister received 3,000 biometric enrolment kits on 1 April 2025, with a second 3,000 expected, to begin constituting the electoral file under PN-RAVEC.
The national director of political and electoral affairs said the biometric census would constitute the national register of natural persons and the electoral file simultaneously.

facts.fact: Guinea's government received 3,000 biometric enrolment kits on 1 April 2025 to begin enrolment for the national register of natural persons and ID cards.
The government said the kits, with fingerprint sensors and iris recognition, guarantee the uniqueness of each citizen.

GIN.note: Gendarmerie chief of staff attended; nothing on station records.

facts.fact: The government said the biometric census under PN-RAVEC, launched with 3,000 kits received on 1 April 2025, would constitute the national register of natural persons.
